reviewer: Fresh independent SCI/ZHEN reviewer; this session performed no authorship or canonical edits.

binding.method: Read the eight requested current JSON files and two recovery records; freeze their exact bytes once using exclusive creation; verify snapshot hashes and current-input hashes. No source page observation was repeated.

structural_checks.source_identity: id/card_id remain phy10-c3-s1; number remains null; original printed heading and source position are retained. This is the unnumbered introduction, not a newly numbered section.

blocks.assessment: Both versions preserve the conceptual sequence: atoms have internal structure; explaining atomic spectra quantitatively helped drive the discovery of quantum-mechanical laws for microscopic particles. This is an appropriate high-level historical summary, not a claim that a single experiment established quantum mechanics or that classical mechanics suffices for microscopic motion.
blocks.source_to_modern_revision: The source's sweeping claim about the most important stage and its repeated statement of later influence are condensed into a measured statement that the discovery helped shape modern physics. The quantitative-theory, spectra and quantum-mechanics meanings remain.
evidence: rutherford-nobel-biography:research paragraph on Bohr, Planck and Heisenberg
blocks.evidence_limit: The Nobel biography corroborates the historical bridge between atomic structure and quantum theory; it is not treated as a primary derivation of quantum mechanics.

blocks.assessment: Both versions correctly identify J. J. Thomson as the electron-discovering physicist and describe his early model as positive charge uniformly distributed through the atom with embedded electrons. The hydrogen sphere and multiple-electron cake/raisin analogy are explicitly scoped to that model. Both subsequently say the historical model failed to describe atomic structure when tested experimentally; neither presents the positive sphere as a modern fact about hydrogen.

radius_and_math.unit: centimeters in the source and both modern locales
radius_and_math.checks: The minus sign, exponent, approximation, radius rather than diameter, centimeter unit and one-electron count are retained. No conversion, new measured value, nucleus radius or electron radius is substituted.

blocks.source_to_modern_revision: The source's categorical first-atomic-model wording becomes an early model, avoiding an overbroad historical priority claim while preserving the named model. Historical and failed-model framing is made explicit.

blocks.assessment: Both versions retain Rutherford's importance for understanding atomic structure and the invitation to examine the experiments more closely. Explaining that experiments test different atomic models is scientifically appropriate. The English Ernest Rutherford and Chinese source surname refer to the same person, not Thomson or a fictional substitute.
blocks.attribution_note: Rutherford's experiments is acceptable shorthand for his research program here; the text does not claim he alone physically performed every measurement. His 1911 paper explicitly credits Geiger and Marsden. No sole-experimenter claim or new experimental detail is introduced.
blocks.source_to_modern_revision: The source's honorific, national descriptor and prerequisite seventh-grade-course comparison are removed. The future invitation and scientific purpose are preserved without asserting a different school prerequisite.

blocks.equivalence: The two-sentence Chinese and English versions agree on complex internal structure, quantitative explanation of atomic spectra, microscopic particles and quantum mechanics. Quantitative does not become qualitative; atomic spectra does not become nuclear spectra.
blocks.child_readability: Both use shorter sentences than the source, preserve the necessary STEM terms and give the same logical sequence. Neither adds an unsupported prerequisite or an extra scientific claim.

blocks.equivalence: Early model, uniform positive-charge distribution, embedded electrons, simplest hydrogen atom, approximate radius of $10^{-8}$ centimeters, one electron, several electrons in more complex atoms, cake/raisins and later experimental rejection all align. The Chinese surname and English J. J. Thomson preserve identity; British matches the source descriptor. Historical-entity declarations bind the retained names to source terms.
blocks.child_readability: Both give the model before the analogy and then explicitly reject it as an account of actual atomic structure. The Chinese plural pronoun in the analogy naturally refers to the immediately preceding electrons, and English makes the same comparison. Paragraph breaks support the shift from describing the model to testing it.

blocks.equivalence: Both say Rutherford's experiments were important and will be examined more closely to understand how they test atomic-structure models. Ernest is the English form of the source's given name. Neither edition carries forward the source's seventh-grade-course dependency or introduces a new grade level.
blocks.child_readability: Both end with a concrete, short invitation to examine evidence and compare models, rather than the source's praise and assumed prior course history.

ZHEN.title_and_locale_assessment: The current Chinese source identity title is retained; the English title is Introduction, with explicit zh/en locales on lesson and exercises. Printed Chinese heading and chapter/section provenance in the English JSON are source metadata, not a mistranslated prose block.

source_to_modern: All three source blocks remain one-to-one and in order in both editions, with shorter modern sentences.
Overbroad historical priority and superlative phrasing are moderated without losing the atomic-structure and quantum-mechanics teaching purpose.
Thomson's hydrogen sphere is explicitly a historical model and its experimental failure is explicit in both languages.
The seventh-grade invitation is localized into a forward-looking explanation of model testing.
The source radius, mathematical token and scientist identities are retained.

scientific_evidence.method: Attempt web search, read the scientific source pages using sequential cloak-fetch text-only calls, and independently confirm source links through Bing when initial searches returned no usable links. Each source-page rendered-text response was snapshotted once, hashed and made read-only; all three responses reported HTTP 200.

url_discovery.limit: Initial URL-discovery attempts were unsuccessful; Bing confirmed the source links afterward. This is a discovery-order limitation, not missing scientific page evidence. Search snippets and AI summaries were not relied on for SCI.

sources.type: HTML transcription of primary 1911 paper, not an original journal scan
sources.used_for: Uniform-charge Thomson model, experimental incompatibility with large deflections, atomic-radius order of magnitude and Geiger/Marsden attribution.
Joseph John Thomson identity and discovery of the electron.
Ernest Rutherford identity, atomic-structure research context and the historical bridge to quantum theory.

scientific_evidence.limits: The Rutherford transcription was read as scientific evidence, not used to redo textbook-source observations or silently correct source math. Unrelated equations and historical numerical estimates from that paper are not imported into this lesson.
